newsitem.title: UK: Whitbread half year profits jump 14 percent.
newsitem.headline: Whitbread half year profits jump 14 percent.

text.p: British brewer to leisure group Whitbread Plc posted a 14 percent increase in its half year profits on Tuesday to 177.5 million pounds ($290.6 million) and chairman Sir Michael Angus said he expects recent levels of growth in its markets to continue.

"We expect the recent levels of growth in our markets to continue as high levels of investment in new and improved outlets attract new customers," said Sir Michael. "Our trading results for the first six months confirm that consumer spending is on an upward trend and I expect this to continue," he added.
Whitbread half year profits jump 14 percent

The company's restaurant and leisure division saw pretax profits rise 58 percent to 56.3 million pounds helped by the recent acquisition of Scott's hotels, sports and healthclub group David Lloyd Leisure and Costa Coffee.

The division includes TGI Friday, Pizza Hut, 50 percent owned by Pepsico, Thresher and Beefeater restaurants as well as 16 Marriot hotels and 130 low budget Travel Inns. Whitbread Inns, which includes casual dining out pub chain Brewers Fayre, profits grew by 15 percent to 77.4 million and total sales by 14 percent, but sales from the company's 2,200 leased pub estate were down three percent.

Whitbread's beer company increased profits by 12 percent to 30.8 million pounds on sales which were ahead eight percent pushed higher by the acquisition of the Labatt and Wadworth brands. Heineken Export and Stella Artois produced the strongest brand performances.

Gearing, however, -- the ratio of debt to equity -- more than doubled to 27.3 percent, after a spate of recent acquisitions including the Pelican Group of French-style urban bistros Cafe Rouge and Dome, for 133 million stg in July.
